title: Quasi-fundamental domain
body_html:
Quasi-fundamental domain

Let $G$ act cellularly on a regular CW complex $X$.

Definition (fundamental domain). A subcomplex $X' \subseteq X$ is a fundamental domain for the $G$-action if the natural map $[\![X']\!] \to G \backslash [\![X]\!]$ is a bijection.

Definition (quasi-fundamental domain, QFD). A subcomplex $X' \subseteq X$ is a quasi-fundamental domain for the $G$-action if there exists a subgroup $G' \le G$ stabilizing $X'$ such that $$G' \backslash [\![X']\!] \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; G \backslash [\![X]\!]$$ is a bijection. We then say the $G'$-set $X'$ is a QFD of the $G$-set $X$.

From the definition, $G' \le \Stab_G(X')$ and the map factors through $G'\backslash[\![X']\!] \to \Stab_G(X')\backslash[\![X']\!]$, so we may always take $G' = \Stab_G(X')$.

Canonical examples

Each item is a QFD of the preceding one:

  1. The $G$-set $\mathcal{B}(G)$, the extended Bruhat–Tits building of $G$ (with a suitable facet structure).
  2. The $N$-set $A$, where $N$ is the normalizer of a maximal split torus $S$ of $G$ and $A \subset \mathcal{B}(G)$ is the corresponding apartment.
  3. The $\Omega$-set $\bar C$, where $\bar C := \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_{A,A^{\mathrm{red}}}(\overline{C'})$ is the preimage of a closed alcove $C'$ in the reduced apartment and $\Omega := \Stab_N(C')$. Equivalently, $\bar C$ is a fundamental domain for the (non-extended) affine Weyl group $W^{\mathrm{aff}}$ acting on $A$.

The third example is developed further in Quasi-fundamental domain from a closed alcove (App B).
